package_info.why_malicious: SHARPTEXT is a malicious browser extension attributed to the SharpTongue (Kimsuky) threat actor. It is specifically engineered to covertly steal webmail credentials, session tokens, and email content from Gmail and AOL users. The extension abuses browser APIs to monitor user activity, extract sensitive data from webmail sessions, and exfiltrate this information to attacker-controlled infrastructure, thereby compromising user privacy and security.

execution_context.trigger: When the user visits Gmail or AOL webmail pages during normal browsing sessions

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user visits Gmail or AOL webmail pages during normal browsing sessions, the extension's background script intercepts web requests to these domains, injects code to extract the entire page content (including emails and credentials), and sends this data via HTTP POST to an attacker-controlled server, resulting in the exfiltration of sensitive webmail information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The extension covertly monitors user activity on webmail services, extracts sensitive page content without user knowledge, and exfiltrates this data to an external server. This behavior is indicative of credential theft and espionage.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate browser extensions should never access or transmit private webmail content without explicit user consent. This extension operates without user awareness, violating privacy and security best practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some security or productivity extensions may request access to webmail pages to provide features like email management or phishing protection, but these actions are always performed with clear user consent and never involve exfiltrating data to unknown external domains.
key_indicators: Accessing and extracting webmail page content (e.g., document.body.innerHTML) from Gmail or AOL domains
Intercepting web requests to mail.google.com and mail.aol.com using webRequest API
Injecting scripts into active webmail tabs via tabs.executeScript
Sending HTTP POST requests containing webmail data to non-legitimate, attacker-controlled domains
Requiring broad permissions such as webRequest, tabs, storage, and activeTab

attack_chain.action: User is deceived into installing the SHARPTEXT browser extension from a web store or phishing link.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious extension is installed and loaded in the user's browser.

attack_chain.action: The extension monitors browser activity for visits to Gmail or AOL webmail domains.
attack_chain.leads_to: Detection of webmail sessions triggers malicious routines.

attack_chain.action: The extension injects code into the webmail tab to extract page content, including emails and credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive webmail data is collected from the user's session.

attack_chain.action: The extension exfiltrates the collected webmail data to attacker-controlled infrastructure via HTTP POST requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains unauthorized access to the user's webmail data and credentials.

behavioral_signatures: Browser extension accessing and extracting content from Gmail or AOL webmail pages
Use of webRequest and tabs APIs to monitor and interact with webmail sessions
Unusual outbound HTTP POST requests from browser extensions to non-legitimate domains
Injection of scripts into webmail tabs without user interaction
file_indicators: Presence of SHARPTEXT extension in browser extension directories
background.js or content scripts containing references to mail.google.com or mail.aol.com
Extension manifest requesting webRequest, tabs, storage, and activeTab permissions
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP POST requests from browser processes to attacker-controlled domains such as attacker-c2.com/collect
Network traffic from browser extensions to unknown or suspicious external endpoints, especially during webmail sessions
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor installed browser extensions for suspicious permissions (webRequest, tabs, storage, activeTab) and behaviors, such as accessing or extracting content from webmail domains. Analyze extension code for references to Gmail or AOL domains and for routines that exfiltrate data. Use network monitoring to detect outbound HTTP POST requests from browser processes to non-legitimate domains, particularly those occurring during webmail sessions. Flag extensions that inject scripts into webmail tabs or transmit webmail content externally without user consent.
